topic: SIPRI Report: India as 2nd Largest Arms Importer

subtopics.title: SIPRI and global arms transfers
subtopics.summary: The Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI), an independent research institute, released the Trends in International Arms Transfers 2025 report on global defence trade. International arms transfers rose 9.2% in 2021-25 compared with 2016-20. The rise in European arms imports, up 210%, was largely driven by the Russia-Ukraine war.
facts: SIPRI: Stockholm International Peace Research Institute, established 1966
SIPRI headquarters: Stockholm, Sweden
SIPRI focus areas: Conflict and Peace Studies; Armaments and Military Expenditure; Arms Transfers and Disarmament
International arms transfers rose 9.2% (2021-25 vs 2016-20)
Arms imports by European countries rose 210%
Rise in European imports largely driven by the Russia-Ukraine war

subtopics.title: Top global exporters and importers
subtopics.summary: The SIPRI report ranks the largest arms exporters and importers for 2021-25. The United States led exports with a 42% share, while Ukraine topped imports with a 9.7% share. Russia's arms exports fell sharply, cutting its share of global exports.
facts: Top exporter: United States, 42% share
Next exporters in order: France, Russia, Germany, China
Russia's arms exports declined by 64%
Russia's share of global exports fell to 6.8%
Top importer: Ukraine, 9.7% share
India ranked second among importers, with an 8.2% share

subtopics.title: India as 2nd largest arms importer
subtopics.summary: India remained the second-largest arms importer during 2021-25, with an 8.2% share. Its overall arms imports fell by 4%, largely due to increased domestic defence manufacturing and indigenisation. Russia, France and Israel were its main suppliers.
facts: India's import rank in 2021-25: 2nd largest
India's share of global arms imports: 8.2%
India's overall arms imports declined by 4%
Decline largely due to domestic manufacturing and indigenisation efforts
India's supplier composition: Russia 40%
India's supplier composition: France 29%
India's supplier composition: Israel 15%

subtopics.title: India's push for domestic defence
subtopics.summary: India has set production and export targets for 2029 and is building its domestic defence capacity. Policy changes, defence industrial corridors and foreign investment rules support this aim. The top three export destinations are the US, France and Armenia.
facts: Defence budget 2026-27: Rs 7.85 lakh crore
Defence production 2024-25: Rs 1.54 lakh crore (2029 target: Rs 3 lakh crore)
Defence exports 2024-25: Rs 23,622 crore (2029 target: Rs 50,000 crore)
Top 3 export destinations: US, France, Armenia
Defence Acquisition Procedure 2020 prioritises Indian-made products over foreign purchases
Defence Industrial Corridors established in Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu
FDI: 74% through automatic route; 100% through government route
iDEX supports startups and MSMEs in defence innovation

quizzes.passage: The Stockholm International Peace Research Institute, known as SIPRI, is an independent international research institute. It has its headquarters in Stockholm, Sweden. Its focus areas include conflict and peace studies, armaments and military expenditure, arms transfers and disarmament. The institute released a report titled Trends in International Arms Transfers 2025, which analyses global defence trade patterns. The report covers international arms transfers during the 2021-25 period and compares them with the 2016-20 period. Among its key global findings, international arms transfers increased over the comparison period, while arms imports by European countries rose sharply, a rise the report largely links to the Russia-Ukraine war. The report also records that arms exports from Russia declined, reducing its share of global exports. The United States is shown as the top exporter, followed by France, Russia, Germany and China. The findings are presented as a set of key global findings, followed by specific findings for India. India is discussed as one of the major importers in the report, and its arms imports are examined for the 2021-25 period. The analysis covers the countries that supply India and the trends in its overall import volumes. Taken together, the report provides a broad view of how weapons move between countries, and it places India within this wider pattern of global defence trade.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A

quizzes.passage: India has several government initiatives in its defence sector, which the report describes under the heading of efforts to reduce arms imports. The government has announced a defence budget for the 2026-27 year, and the report records the value of defence production and exports for the year 2024-25. Targets have also been set for production and exports for the year 2029. Policy steps are aimed at building a domestic defence manufacturing ecosystem, and special industrial zones are being developed to support this aim. The rules for foreign investment in defence are structured in two parts, one for investment through the automatic route and another through the government route. Innovation in the sector is also an area of focus under the government programmes. The top three destinations for Indian defence exports are named in the report. The report sets out these figures as part of the country efforts to build its defence capacity, and the initiatives are presented together so that production, exports, investment and innovation can be read as one set of measures. Together, these measures show how the country is trying to expand its own capacity to produce defence equipment while reducing its reliance on arms bought from other countries.
